page: Amazon Web Services r5d.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results position the r5d.12xlarge primarily in the average tier for multi-core and memory operations. While single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by bottom-tier stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression scores, its multi-core capabilities are more robust, achieving average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks consistently fall within the middle 50% of tested systems. Database operations and Redis SET performance also align with average tier expectations.

The presence of 1800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage combined with 384.0 GB of RAM makes this instance highly suitable for memory-intensive workloads that require fast local scratch space or caching, such as relational databases, in-memory analytics, and medium-scale data processing. However, the single-threaded performance bottleneck represents a clear tradeoff, making it less optimal for single-core bound applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r5d.12xlarge offers a dense allocation of memory and high-speed local storage on a dedicated CPU model, balancing resource density against moderate compute performance.
